extracted.intended_audience: NICHD/NIH grant applicants, institutional research administrators, and NICHD program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Operating guidelines and decision criteria NICHD used in FY2022 to allocate grant funds across mechanisms, including paylines, budget adjustments, program priorities (e.g., Early Stage Investigators), and policy constraints (salary caps, future-year commitments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall funding objective and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD is committed to funding the largest number of meritorious projects possible, while allowing flexibility to fund selected program priorities and respond to emerging scientific opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources are distributed among diverse programs and mechanisms; funding decisions will reflect the NICHD Strategic Plan and emerging opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriation with adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: General guidelines for funding were established based on the NIH appropriation for the fiscal year, with allowances for necessary adjustments throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments may reflect directives from Congress and NIH, as well as emerging program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for Next Generation Researchers / Early Stage Investigators (ESI)
rubrics_metrics.description: NICHD will include ESI investigator status as one of the program priorities when considering funding of eligible applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows NIH Policy Supporting the Next Generation Researchers Initiative (NOT-OD-17-101 and NOT-OD-18-214). ESI status is considered alongside other program priorities in funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to requested budget levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments to requested budgets may be necessary to award as many grants as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors motivating reductions include: a significant increase in the size of budget requests; a large and growing commitment base for ongoing grants; and limited growth in the NICHD budget to accommodate those factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: R01 (Research Project) funding reductions and considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For all new competing R01 (Type 1) applications selected for funding, NICHD will reduce awards on average by 14 percent below the peer review recommended level of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final reductions may vary depending on research scope, comments in the summary statement, availability of other support, and program priorities. There is no fixed payline for R01s; NICHD will consider scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 and R21 (Small/Exploratory) payline policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed payline for R03 or R21 applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NICHD will consider scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and availability of funds when making funding decisions for these mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: AREA (R15) payline
rubrics_metrics.description: The FY2022 payline for R15 (AREA) applications is Priority Score 32.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR and SBIR payline policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed payline for STTR (R41, R42) and SBIR (R43, R44) applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NICHD will consider scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and availability of funds when making funding decisions for these small business mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development (K) paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: The FY2022 payline for competing K applications is Priority Score 24, with a differential payline for K99 applications of Priority Score 34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/Workshop (R13/U13) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed payline for R13/U13 applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NICHD will consider scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and availability of funds for these awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Fellowship (F) paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: FY2022 paylines: F30 Priority Score 29; parent F31 at the 26th percentile; Diversity F31 at the 33rd percentile; F32 at the 33rd percentile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Training (T32) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no fixed payline for T32 applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding consideration will include scientific merit, program priorities, portfolio balance, and availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other mechanisms (R24, U24, R25) paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: FY2022 paylines: R24 and U24 Priority Score 21; R25 Priority Score 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of legislated salary limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislated salary limitation for grants applies to both competing and non-competing grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current limitations were published in February 2022 (NOT-OD-22-076).

rubrics_metrics.name: Future year commitments and escalation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Inflationary increases for future year commitments are no longer provided for all competing and non-competing research grant awards issued by NICHD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments for special needs (such as equipment and added personnel) continue to be accommodated when justified. Modular grants do not receive escalation in future years. See NOT-OD-13-064 and modular application guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-competing continuation (Type 5) support level and stipend policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-competing FY2022 level of support is presented on the FY2021 award notice and generally reflects no cost of living/inflationary adjustments; NICHD will support FY2022 awards at 100%. Non-competing Fellowship (F) and Training (T) grants will reflect current FY stipend levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipend levels may be adjusted as appropriate.
